The FY2020 revenue figure originally reported in IBM's FY2020 10-K ($73,620 million) [DOC-1] is **not directly comparable** to the FY2022 figure ($60,530 million) [DOC-2], because IBM completed the spin-off of its managed infrastructure services unit (Kyndryl Holdings, Inc.) on November 3, 2021, and restated historical results to present Kyndryl as discontinued operations [DOC-3]. As a result, the FY2022 10-K itself provides a restated, comparable FY2020 revenue figure of $55,179 million (continuing operations basis) [DOC-2], rather than the originally reported $73,620 million.

Using the comparable (continuing operations) basis presented in the FY2022 filing:

- FY2020 revenue (restated, continuing operations): $55,179 million [DOC-2]
- FY2022 revenue: $60,530 million [DOC-2]
- Growth = ($60,530M − $55,179M) / $55,179M ≈ 9.7%

If instead one used the originally reported FY2020 figure of $73,620 million [DOC-1] (which includes Kyndryl operations later divested), revenue would appear to have *declined* by about 17.8% — but this comparison would be misleading given the change in reporting basis due to the divestiture.

ANSWER: On a comparable (continuing operations) basis, IBM's revenue grew approximately 9.7%, from $55,179 million in FY2020 (restated) to $60,530 million in FY2022. Note: the originally reported FY2020 revenue of $73,620 million is not comparable to FY2022 due to the Kyndryl spin-off, which caused IBM to restate historical results to exclude discontinued operations.
